issues.legal_issue: A referring authority may make a statutory land-acquisition reference only when the statutory conditions, including timely application, are satisfied.
material_facts: The award was communicated to the landowner, who first sought review from the land-acquisition officer rather than applying for a court reference.
After the review request was refused, the landowner applied for a reference outside the statutory two-month period.
The landowner sought to exclude the time spent in the review proceedings when calculating limitation.
issues.conclusion: The reference application was time-barred, and the review proceedings did not make it timely. The conditions for a valid reference were not satisfied.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 14(1) and 15 of the Hyderabad Land Acquisition Act, corresponding to sections 18(1) and 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the referring authority's power is conditional on compliance with the statutory requirements, particularly the time limit in section 18(2)'s proviso. A timely application is a sine qua non of a valid reference. The Court upheld the lower courts' conclusion that section 14 of the Limitation Act did not assist the landowner and that, in any event, the required good faith had not been established. The Court applied the principles concerning statutory tribunals in The Queen v. Commissioners for Special Purposes of the Income Tax, Jagdish Prasad v. Ganga Prasad, and Nusserwanjee Pestonjee v. Meer Mynoodeen Khan.

predicates.statutory_land_acquisition_reference: The proceeding seeks a court determination through a statutory land-acquisition reference.
predicates.referring_authority_power_depends_on_sta: The law makes the referring authority's power dependent on compliance with specified statutory conditions.
predicates.application_was_outside_deadline: The person seeking the reference applied after the applicable statutory time limit.

issues.definition: When a statutory land-acquisition reference is sought under a scheme that conditions the referring authority's power on compliance with statutory requirements, an application outside the deadline results in an invalid reference.

issues.legal_issue: A court exercising special statutory jurisdiction over a land-acquisition reference must determine whether the reference satisfies the conditions that confer jurisdiction, and may refuse to answer an invalid reference.
material_facts: The land-acquisition officer referred the matter to the court without expressing an opinion on whether the reference application was time-barred.
The reference had been made on an application submitted after the statutory deadline.
The government challenged the reference as incompetent, and the lower courts declined to entertain it.
issues.conclusion: The court was entitled and required to examine the reference's validity, including whether the application was timely. Having found the application time-barred, it could decline to answer the reference.
issues.legal_principle: A tribunal whose jurisdiction is specially and narrowly conferred by statute must ensure that the conditions for exercising that jurisdiction have been met. Sections 18 to 21 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, limit the court's jurisdiction over a reference; a proper reference under section 18 is required before the court can hear it. The Court applied The Queen v. Commissioners for Special Purposes of the Income Tax, Jagdish Prasad v. Ganga Prasad, and Nusserwanjee Pestonjee v. Meer Mynoodeen Khan, and approved the principle that a tribunal must verify the facts on which its jurisdiction depends.

predicates.statutory_land_acquisition_reference: The proceeding asks a court to hear a reference made under a statutory land-acquisition scheme.
predicates.court_has_special_limited_jurisdiction: The court's authority to hear the matter is specially and narrowly defined by statute.
predicates.reference_was_based_on_late_application: The reference was made on an application submitted after the applicable statutory deadline.

issues.definition: When a court with special, limited jurisdiction receives a statutory land-acquisition reference based on a late application, it may decline to answer the reference.
